items.followUp: Define a covalent bond and state four properties of covalent compounds.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed by electron transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition involving attraction between oppositely charged ions; electron transfer may also be stated.

rubric.why: The question asks for four properties; each correct property earns 1 mark.
rubric.description: Gives four properties of ionic compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each distinct correct property, up to 4. Accept any four, including crystalline nature, high melting/boiling points, water solubility, brittleness, and electrical conduction when molten or in aqueous solution.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed by the transfer of electrons.
Ionic compounds are crystalline solids.
They generally have high melting and boiling points.
They are usually soluble in water.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but not in the solid state.

items.followUp: Define evaporation and describe how temperature, surface area and wind affect its rate.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the movement or spreading of particles from higher to lower concentration.

rubric.why: The answer must describe the effect of any three factors, not merely name them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each correctly described factor, up to 3. Accept effects of temperature, concentration gradient, particle size/mass, or the medium.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Increasing temperature increases the kinetic energy of particles, so diffusion becomes faster.
A steeper concentration gradient makes diffusion faster.
Smaller or lighter particles diffuse faster than larger or heavier particles.

items.followUp: State four differences between a true solution and a suspension.

rubric.why: These are standard characteristics of a solution; each relevant characteristic earns credit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each correct characteristic, up to 2. Accept any characteristics listed in the second rubric point as well.

rubric.why: Two further correct characteristics complete the requested four.
rubric.description: States further characteristics of a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each additional correct characteristic, up to 2; do not award twice for the same property.

modelAnswer: A solution is a homogeneous mixture with uniform composition throughout.
Its solute particles are extremely small and cannot be seen with the naked eye.
The solute particles do not settle on standing, so the solution is stable.
The particles pass through filter paper and cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.

items.followUp: Define relative molecular mass and explain what is meant by its gram molecular mass.

rubric.why: Relative atomic mass is defined by comparison with one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the comparison of an atom's average mass with 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

rubric.why: The relative atomic mass expressed in grams is the gram atomic mass, i.e. the mass of one mole of the atoms.
rubric.description: Relates relative atomic mass to grams.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its numerical value in grams is the gram atomic mass or the mass of one mole of those atoms.

modelAnswer: Relative atomic mass is the average mass of an atom of an element compared with 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
When the relative atomic mass is expressed in grams, it is called the gram atomic mass and is the mass of one mole of the atoms.

items.followUp: Differentiate between molecular mass and gram molecular mass.

rubric.why: Molecular mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in a molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly defining molecular mass as the sum of the atomic masses in a molecule.

rubric.why: Formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses represented by an ionic compound's formula unit, rather than a molecule.
rubric.description: Defines formula mass and distinguishes it from molecular mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying formula mass as the sum of atomic masses in a formula unit, generally for an ionic compound.

modelAnswer: Molecular mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in one molecule, usually of a covalent compound.
Formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms or ions represented by one formula unit, usually of an ionic compound.

items.followUp: Write two differences between a cation and an anion.

rubric.why: An ion is charged because it has gained or lost electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying an ion as a charged atom or group formed by gaining or losing electrons.

rubric.why: A free radical is characterized by one or more unpaired electrons; this distinguishes it from the general definition of an ion.
rubric.description: Describes a free radical and distinguishes it from an ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a free radical has one or more unpaired electrons. Accept that it may exist independently.

modelAnswer: An ion is an atom or group of atoms with a positive or negative charge because it has lost or gained electrons.
A free radical is an atom or group of atoms containing one or more unpaired electrons and capable of independent existence.

items.followUp: State two properties of an electron beam that show it is negatively charged.

rubric.why: Cathode rays travel in straight lines and can produce fluorescence or cast shadows.
rubric.description: States one characteristic property of cathode rays.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct property, such as straight-line travel, fluorescence, or casting shadows.

rubric.why: Cathode rays are negatively charged and are deflected by electric or magnetic fields; their properties are also independent of the gas and cathode material.
rubric.description: States a second property of cathode rays.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct correct property. Accept any valid property, including deflection toward the positive plate or independence from the gas or cathode.

modelAnswer: Cathode rays travel in straight lines.
They carry a negative charge and are deflected toward the positive plate in an electric field.

items.followUp: State Mendeleev's periodic law and explain one limitation of his periodic table.

rubric.why: Newlands arranged elements in order of increasing atomic mass.
rubric.description: Describes the arrangement of elements in Newlands' law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that elements were arranged in order of increasing atomic mass.

rubric.why: The properties of every eighth element were similar to those of the first, like notes in a musical octave.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, or making the correct musical-octave comparison.

modelAnswer: Newlands arranged the known elements in order of increasing atomic mass.
He observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, like the repetition of notes in a musical octave.
